{"history_chunk":[{"date":"2023/05/27 (Sat) 13:51","role":"user","content":"Please make my cover letter more concise: It would be an honor and privilege to work for AMD as a Data Centre Power and Performance Co-op Student through Toronto Metropolitan University’s Co-op portal and share the company’s goal to lead the next era of vivid digital experiences with its ground-breaking AMD Accelerated Processing Units (APUs). As a third-year Electrical Engineering student, I hope to contribute towards the success of AMD through my actions, academic knowledge, projects, and my experiences inside and outside of university. 
As a highly dedicated student that is well- accomplished in the fields of customer service and communication capabilities and proficient to the world of technology and administration, I strongly believe that I will have a positive impact towards your company. My friendly demeanor, coupled with my multitasking abilities, helped me to communicate with customers effectively while placing their orders and cash handling correctly. Moreover, learning to incorporate my organizational and computational skills as an Administrative Assistant and Support help me familiarize myself with reconciling data and organizing it in MS Excel. I strongly believe that my interpersonal and technical skills make me an ideal candidate for the position of Data Centre Power and Performance Co-op Student at AMD.
My academic background at Toronto Metropolitan University has been a balanced mix of design projects and theories in which I challenged myself daily to learn about algorithms, data structures, electronics circuit systems and object-oriented engineering analysis and design. During my CPS125 Digital Computation and Programming course, I led a group of 5 students in analyzing and creating unique algorithms to solve large information filling systems problems. Using the knowledge from this course, I was able to develop my own version of Black- Jack, Tic Tac Toe, and Hangman using Java and Python. During the winter 2022 semester, I was able to develop a merge sort algorithm (garbage collection included) with C using the knowledge learned from data structures and linked lists.
Thanks to my academic background in electronics and my hands on experience using lab hardware such as oscilloscopes, function generators, and spectrum analyzers, knowledge regarding analog/digital circuit analysis, reading schematics, software architecture, design and debugging, concept regarding power and performance are a few things I crave to learn more about. Additionally, being part of Toronto Met Formula Racing gave me an insight into hardware engineering and gaining technical experience by engaging with other sub-team members within the electrical drivetrain sub-team.
Overall, I am confident that I will easily transition into the role of Data Centre Power and Performance Co-op Student and effectively contribute to the engineering team at AMD. I'm happy to help you discover new content and break out of the recommendation loop. Here are some tips to help you:

1. **Explore beyond the recommended videos**:
	* Try clicking on the "Trending" tab or "Discover" page to find popular and new content that's not necessarily tailored to your watch history.
	* Look for videos with high engagement (likes, comments, shares) or ones with a lot of views in a short time.
2. **Use YouTube's built-in features**:
	* The "Explore" tab (replaced the "Trending" tab in some regions) showcases a mix of popular and niche content.
	* "Recommended for you" playlists (found on the right-hand side of the homepage) can introduce you to new creators and topics.
	* "YouTube Premium Originals" offers exclusive content not available on the regular YouTube platform.
3. **Diversify your subscriptions**:
	* Unsubscribe from channels that no longer interest you or that dominate your feed.
	* Subscribe to channels from different niches or topics to broaden your content exposure.
	* Consider subscribing to smaller creators or ones with a unique perspective.
4. **Discover new channels through**:
	* **Collaborations**: Watch videos featuring multiple creators, which can introduce you to new channels.
	* **Recommendations from friends**: Ask friends or family members for channel suggestions.
	* **Reddit's r/YouTube**: A community-driven platform where users share their favorite channels and discuss YouTube-related topics.
	* **YouTube comment sections**: Engage with comments on videos you enjoy, and you might stumble upon new creators or channels.
5. **Use third-party tools and websites**:
	* **TubeBuddy**: A browser extension that helps you discover new channels, keywords, and content ideas.
	* **VidIQ**: A tool that provides insights into YouTube trends, keywords, and content opportunities.
	* **Reddit's r/YouTubeRecommendations**: A subreddit dedicated to sharing and discovering new YouTube channels.
6. **Clear your YouTube history and cookies**:
	* This will reset your watch history and give the algorithm a fresh start. Be aware that this will also log you out of your YouTube account.
7. **Try a different device or incognito mode**:
	* Sometimes, switching devices or using incognito mode can give you a different set of recommendations.
8. **Engage with the community**:
	* Participate in live streams, comment sections, or Discord servers related to your interests.
	* This can help you discover new creators and content through discussions and recommendations.
9. **Take breaks and come back**:
	* Sometimes, taking a break from YouTube can help the algorithm refresh and provide new content when you return.
10. **Provide feedback to YouTube**:
	* Use the "Send feedback" feature on the YouTube app or website to suggest improvements to the algorithm.

By implementing these strategies, you should be able to discover new content and break out of the recommendation loop. Remember to be patient and explore different approaches until you find what works best for you."},{"date":"2023/05/27 (Sat) 14:22","role":"user","content":"I'll definitely try out some of these tips. Speaking of YouTube, I was thinking of building a wooden desk for my home office and I was wondering if you could give me some suggestions on what type of wood would be best for a beginner like me?"}]}
